meta.title: Code for Battle — Browser real-time strategy
meta.description: Code for Battle is a tile-based real-time strategy game in the browser. Build a powered base, harvest ore, and command tanks, jets, and a navy.

hero.title: Code for Battle
hero.tagline: Command the battlefield from your browser.
hero.lead: Raise a powered base, harvest ore, and send tanks, jets, and a fleet into the same fight. A tile-based RTS that starts immediately, with nothing to install.

features.title: In the current build
features.lead: Everything on this page is in the game today.

economy.title: Base economy
economy.body: Power plants, ore fields, and refineries pay for production. Orders run through queues, rally points, and stacked build commands.

tech.title: Unlock tree
tech.body: Factories, radar, and the shipyard open new vehicles, guns, aircraft, and ships. Fresh options appear in the production sidebar.

arms.title: Land, air, and sea
arms.body: Field tank variants, rocket tanks, and howitzers. Hold ground with gun, rocket, tesla, and artillery turrets. Launch an Apache, an F-22, and an F-35. Put to sea with a destroyer, battleship, carrier, submarine, hovercraft, ferry, supply ship, and mine layers.

logistics.title: Supply and crews
logistics.body: Fuel and ammunition run out. Tankers, ammo trucks, the hospital, and ambulances keep units fighting. Mines, sweepers, and recovery tanks work the field. Promotions improve range, armor, or rate of fire.

command.title: Command
command.body: Box-select, assign control groups, queue waypoints, guard friendlies, and drag attack groups. Sell or repair structures, and lay walls and streets. Two gamepads can share one side.

controllers.title: Controllers
controllers.body: Plug in up to two gamepads. Player 1 moves the cursor; player 2 can remote-control another unit of the same side, on or off screen. Mappings and profiles are saved in the browser.

persistence.title: Save and replay
persistence.body: Save and resume a battle in the browser, export the file, or inspect it in the save editor. Record a match and play the command log back.

multiplayer.title: Multiplayer
multiplayer.body: Host an invite link or QR code and let another person join that party over WebRTC. Lockstep keeps both simulations on the same inputs. A dropped link pauses the match until they reconnect.

battlefield.title: Living map
battlefield.body: Generated maps carry biomes, ore, coasts, cliffs, and procedural water. Milestone films mark the first refinery, tank, mine layer, mine sweeper, rocket tank, howitzer, Tesla coil, and airstrip. A loading screen and a phone HUD ship with the game.

workshop.title: Map workshop
workshop.body: Set water, rock, and ore, paint tiles in the map editor, and compose the sprite sheets the battle renders.

vibe.title: Fully vibe-coded
vibe.lead: Code for Battle was built entirely through prompt-driven development. The simulation, the interface, and the production assets were generated, then wired into a playable browser RTS.
vibe.assetsLead: These kinds are in the repository and used by the live game.

units.title: Unit sprites
units.body: Map and sidebar art for vehicles, aircraft, and ships, including separate turrets and barrels.

buildings.title: Building sprites
buildings.body: Map and sidebar art for factories, defenses, pads, the airstrip, and the shipyard.

terrain.title: Terrain and tiles
terrain.body: Grass, streets, rock, cliffs, crystals, debris, and biome atlases as sprite sheets.

vfx.title: Explosion animations
vfx.body: Sprite-sheet sequences for destruction and impacts.

ui.title: Interface icons
ui.body: Icons for save, repair, import, and export, plus the command HUD.

cursors.title: Command cursors
cursors.body: Pointers for move, attack, guard, repair, and sell, including blocked and out-of-range states.

sfx.title: Sound effects
sfx.body: Weapons, engines, explosions, construction, and movement.

narrator.title: Narrator voice-over
narrator.body: Spoken reports for orders, attacks, losses, and unit readiness.

video.title: Milestone videos
video.body: Narrated films for the first refinery, tank, mine layer, mine sweeper, rocket tank, howitzer, Tesla coil, and airstrip.

tech.title: Tech tree
tech.lead: Buildings and units unlock as the prerequisites are constructed. The diagram follows the in-game unlock rules and the player guide, including the naval branch.
tech.note: A replacement Construction Yard requires a Vehicle Workshop. The Shipyard must be placed on a shoreline.

groups.openingLead: The match starts with a Construction Yard on the map. Streets can be laid immediately. Power, ore, and a vehicle factory follow, and that factory opens the rest of the base.
groups.buildingsLead: Further structures appear after the buildings on the left are standing.
groups.unitsLead: A unit enters the production sidebar when every requirement on the left is met.

multiplayer.title: Multiplayer
multiplayer.lead: A human can take a party in a match you host. Parties left empty stay with the built-in opponent, and a party can instead be handed to an optional LLM commander.
multiplayer.hostBody: The host creates an invite link and a QR code for one party. The guest opens that link, enters an alias, and connects with WebRTC through the signalling server.
multiplayer.partiesBody: A match can have two, three, or four parties. Each non-host party can be a human invite or stay under AI control.
multiplayer.lockstepBody: When a guest connects, both peers share a session seed and exchange inputs. Periodic state hashes check that the simulations still match. If they diverge, the host can send a full snapshot to resync.
multiplayer.reconnectBody: If the link drops, the match pauses and waits for that player to return. An unresponsive peer does not keep the simulation running ahead alone.
multiplayer.devicesBody: The same invite works from another browser on this computer, or from an iPhone, iPad, or Mac, when the page is the public HTTPS site. Google STUN is always used. A TURN relay is added when the signalling server is configured with one, which is what makes many phone, cellular, and off-network joins possible. A localhost link cannot be opened by a phone, and iPhone or iPad Safari will not start WebRTC on a page that is not a secure context.

controllers.title: Controllers
controllers.lead: The browser Gamepad API drives the same commands as the mouse and keyboard. Two people can share one screen.
controllers.mapBody: Settings lists every button, stick axis, and trigger on each connected controller and lights the row while you press it. Click a command, then press or move the control to bind it. Noise inside the deadzone is ignored. Escape cancels. A conflict names the command that already uses that control.
controllers.profilesBody: A player profile keeps one person's button layout on any controller. A controller-type profile fills only controls that have no standard button or stick, and each physical controller can still keep its own profile. You can save, load, rename, delete, and reset them. Disconnecting does not erase a profile.
controllers.coopBody: Only player 1 moves the cursor. Player 2 claims a unit of the same party and remote-controls it even when it is off screen. The camera eases to the midpoint between the two units, stays with player 1 when player 2 leaves the view, and frames both again when player 2 comes back.
controllers.defaultsBody: Left stick moves the cursor for player 1 and drives player 2's unit. Right stick scrolls the map. Face buttons click, repair, and jump to the last attack notice. Bumpers turn the turret, the right trigger fires, and the d-pad matches the keyboard remote controls.
